items.t: Chapter 13 (al-bāb al-thālith ʿashar): On the letters absent from the noble Fātiḥa (sawāqiṭal-Fātiḥa) and the awfāq and invocations that belong to them [132]

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in the understanding of His names — that the letters (fāʾ),(jīm), (shīn),(thāʾ),(ẓāʾ),(khāʾ) and (zāy) are among the letters absent from the Fātiḥa, and that every one of these letters has a name from among the names of God, exalted is He. The fāʾ has, of the names of God, exalted is He, Fard (the Single); the jīm, Jabbār (the Compeller); the shīn, Shakūr (the Most Thankful); the thāʾ, Thābit (the Firm); the ẓāʾ, Ẓahīr (the Supporter); the khāʾ, Khabīr (the All-Aware); and the zāy, Zakī (the Pure). These seven letters give notice of good and of felicity, and they give notice of torment and of humiliation. As for their giving notice of good: the letter fāʾ — Nay, I swear by the setting-places of the stars; and truly it is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:75–76); and the letter jīm — Gardens of Eden which they shall enter (Q 13:23); and the letter shīn — God bears witness that there is no god but

He (Q 3:18), the verse; and the letter thāʾ — Then We gave the Book in inheritance to those of Our servants whom We chose (Q 35:32); and the letter ẓāʾ — its outward side, in it is mercy, and its inward side, facing it is the torment (cf. Q 57:13, with the two halves inverted); and the letter khāʾ — good and beautiful ones (Q 55:70); and the letter zāy — Made fair-seeming to men is the love of desires (Q 3:14). So when you desire an operation for good, write the letter you wish that is suited to what you seek, and write with it the verse that is suited to that, and the object sought will be attained, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Faṣl. And according to the second view, these expressive letters give notice of torment just as they give notice of good; so you write them for torment as well. They operate upon the seven days, for each of these seven letters has one of the days of the week. Sunday belongs to the Sun, and its servant is Rūqiyāʾīl, and of the terrestrial [kings], the king al-Mudhhib (the Gilded). Monday belongs to the Moon, and its servant is Jibrāʾīl, and of the terrestrial, the king al-Abyaḍ (the White). Tuesday belongs to Mars, and its servant is Samsamāʾīl, and of the terrestrial, the king al-Aḥmar (the Red). Wednesday belongs to Mercury, and its celestial servant is Mīkāʾīl, and of the terrestrial, Burqān. Thursday belongs to Jupiter, and its servant is Ṣarfiyāʾīl, and of the terrestrial, the king Shamhūrash. Friday belongs to Venus, and her celestial servant is ʿAynayāʾīl, and of the terrestrial, the king Zawbaʿa. Saturday belongs to Maymūn — that is, Saturn — and its servant is Kasfiyāʾīl, and of the terrestrial kings, Abā Nūkh. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided. /fol. 82v./

Corrected in this edition: Saturday's king is Maymūn Abū Nūkh. The print has Abā Fūkh — fāʾ for nūn; the book gives Maymūn Abū Nūkh on p.1566 and Abū Nūḥ Maymūn on p.1371. Note also that this page names Monday's king al-Abyaḍ and Friday's Zawbaʿa, where pp.114–115, 920–922 and chapter 20 name them Murra and al-Abyaḍ: the book carries both traditions (see pp.654, 820–821), so that is left as printed.

Faṣl. And these seven letters give notice of torment, so you shall write them for torment as well. You write the seven letters, beginning with the letter shīn, following the succession of the days and their letters; and you reverse the object sought, and you say in your invocation over them: "...unless you do to so-and-so son of so-and-so [woman], or to so-and-so daughter of so-and-so, that which is such and such" — and you name for him whatever you wish of the kinds of afflictions and sicknesses. And [this is done] after the writing of the letters according to its pattern and after the day and the object sought are as they should be. And you say in your invocation: O Shadīd (Severe), O ʿAzīz (Mighty), O Aḥad (Unique), O Ẓāhir (Manifest), O Wārith (Inheritor), O Jabbār (Compeller), O Fāṭir (Originator)! O God, send down upon so-and-so son of so-and-so [woman] such and such. O God, O You who are severe in seizing, O Bāqī (Abiding) after the passing away of His creation, according to the command that He willed and the power that You determined! O You whose existence has no conjoining and no ending! O You whom none of His creation draws near to! O You whose beginninglessness has no beginning and whose everlastingness has no cutting off! On a day when God will not put to shame the Prophet and those who have believed with him (Q 66:8). Surely the shame this day, and the evil, are upon those who disbelieve (Q 16:27). O You who are severe in torment and in punishment! Truly the seizing-grip of your Lord is severe (Q 85:12). And as for those made wretched, they are in the Fire; theirs therein is braying and gasping (Q 11:106). Truly the tree of Zaqqūm is the food of the sinner; like molten dross it boils in the bellies, as scalding water boils (Q 44:43–46). O ʿAzīz, O Ghālib (Prevailer), O You who have no like, and with whom lies the fulfilment of needs, all of them! You are the absolute, beginningless Mighty One; none other than You is Your equal in Your might. O You who are manifest in power! O You who said — and He is the most truthful of speakers — By no means! It is Laẓā, the blaze, that strips away the scalp (Q 70:15–16), affording no shade, and of no avail against the blaze (Q 77:31)! O Wārith, You are the One to whom the affairs and existence return, and to Him the whole affair returns! O You who cause the engendered beings and those within them to pass away, and who calls out: To whom belongs the kingdom this day? To God, the One, the All-Subduing (Q 40:16)! For everyone who has an invocation in a matter, inward or outward, little or much. O God, send down upon so-and-so son of so-and-so [woman] the ruin and the woe and the torment: Do not call this day for a single ruin, but call for many ruins (Q 25:14). O Jabbār, You are the One whose decree passes by way of compulsion upon every one; the wariness of the wary does not repel it. And You indeed are the One to whom [all] returns in sheer subjugation. You have bound the powers of the soul and the powers of the heart within the densities of the bodies by Your highest omnipotence (jabarūt), which has been declared free of imperfection in what is due to

You, and which You made an attribute of Your ipseity, a manifestation of Your subduing-power, and an attribute of Your beginninglessness; for You are the Possessor of power and of omnipotence, of might and of awe. And by the might of Your dominion (malakūt), which You chose by the eye of Your power, and the judgements of Your divinity, and the lights of Your incinerating [powers] — which none but You knows; exalted be Your affair and great Your sovereignty! For every motion in the world of the kingdom (mulk) and of the dominion and of the omnipotence has been encompassed by the meaning of Your name al-Jabbār. By the right of that which You have compelled by the compulsion of the beginningless, majestic, supremely great governance, O You who compelled the human world by its motion, through what is within it of the secret of the life mingled with the spirit, by the reins of the measures /fol. 83r./ and the divine leave, until the world was compelled, one part of it subduing another, for the establishing of subjugation and the manifesting of wisdom: manifest in so-and-so son of so-and-so [woman] such of the severity of Your seizing-grip and Your subduing as shall still his senses when he collides with me and quench his spiritual force (rūḥāniyya) at his presence. Truly Hell is the appointed place for them all (Q 15:43). And We have surely brought into being for Hell many of the jinn and of mankind (Q 7:179). O Fāṭir of the heavens and the earth, I ask You, O God, by Your power with which You originated the celestial and the terrestrial engendered beings, and by the right of the first Word with which You originated the heavens and the earth, by Your true saying: Then He mounted up to heaven, it being smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come, obedient (Q 41:11) — appoint for me that which is such and such (and you name what you wish), for that will come to pass. And these seven letters give notice of torment, just as those seven foregoing letters give notice of good: — and they came to be such that nothing was seen but their dwellings (Q 46:25); — jahannam (Hell) — theirs therein is braying and gasping (Q 11:106);
— a flame of fire and molten brass, and you two will not be helped (Q 55:35); — then He caused him to die and had him buried (Q

80:21); — Corruption has appeared on land and sea (Q 30:41); — God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their eyes is a covering, and theirs is a mighty torment (Q 2:7); — Satan made their deeds fair-seeming to them (Q 8:48). And these serve to drive off, over against what has gone before; so make your analogy upon that and understand, and you will hit the mark.

You say: My Master, I seek Your aid against him who has wronged me; and I ask You, my Master, to give me victory over him who has warred against me, and to rout him who has come out against me, and to subdue him who has fought me, and to forsake my enemies and to subdue them and rout them wherever they gather, and to curse them and disgrace them wherever they separate, and to cut them off and try them wherever they join together, and to consign them to a darkness in which they wander blindly and to an abasement in which they are afflicted; and that from the retribution there be no passing beyond, and that nothing go straight for them, neither in secret nor openly, and that they gain neither might nor glory, and that they be able neither to help nor to endure. And send upon them a torment from above them and from beneath their feet, and clothe them in [warring] sects, and make some of them taste the violence of others, and make them fuel for Hell, and turn their hearts away from uprightness, and give them abundant water to drink, and make their works upon the earth a barren waste, and send upon their gardens a reckoning out of heaven, so that it becomes a slippery bare slope, or its water sinks away (Q 18:40–41); and make them the greatest losers in works, and raise up no head for them, and make them of the fearful, and stretch out for them no arm's span; and make them of the losers, who are able neither to turn aside nor to ransom, and are able neither to drink nor to eat, and are not able to give satisfaction; and drag them with the chains and the shackles, and set before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and on their right an upraised bank and on their left a rampart, and over their heads a rock, and beneath their feet [likewise], so that /fol. 83v./ walking may not be sweet to them; and appoint no good for them, and put the shackles upon their necks, and put the fetters upon their feet, and shake them with earthquakes, with the enemies at their heels, and weary them in the way-stations, that they may not prosper; and overturn their intellects and make them rugged, that they may not comprehend, and invert their spirits, that they may not be guided aright, and cast their souls into despair, that they may not deal justly, and seal up their mouths, that they may not speak, and transform them where they stand, so that they are able neither to go forward nor to return to their people. For truly You are al-Jabbār (the Compeller), al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great), al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), al-Ṭālib (the Pursuer), al-Ghālib (the Prevailer), al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), al-Mudhill (the Giver of abasement), al-Muntaqim (the Avenger), al-Muhlik (the Destroyer), Dhū al-baṭsh al-shadīd (Possessor of the mighty assault), Possessor of the Glorious Throne. God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their eyes is a covering, and theirs is a mighty torment (Q 2:7). God mocks them, and prolongs them in their insolence, wandering blindly (Q 2:15). Deaf, dumb, blind — so they do not return (Q 2:18). Or like a cloudburst out of heaven, in which are darknesses and thunder and lightning: they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderbolts, in fear of death — and God encompasses the unbelievers. The lightning well-nigh snatches away their sight — up to His words — powerful (Q 2:19–20). Abasement is stamped upon them wherever they are come upon, save by a rope from God and a rope from men; and they have incurred wrath from God, and wretchedness is stamped upon them (Q 3:112). And those who disbelieved said to their messengers: We shall surely drive you out — up to His words — the wrongdoers (Q 14:13). Truly We shall help Our messengers and those who have believed — up to His words — the evil abode (Q 40:51–52). So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off; and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 6:45). Then you say what you wish, and it will come to pass in the swiftest time.

The awfāq that pertain to this chapter, without which the operation is not completed — they are the seven squares mentioned, as their mention has already gone before; and every square has one letter of the seven successive letters. And they are as you see.

Know — may God grant me and you success in the understanding of His names — that these seven letters are fiery, and that they are bound up with what we have mentioned before, of the destruction of

— the tyrannical enemies, because they have fallen out of the noble Fātiḥa on account of the evil and the punishment that are in them. And they are. And every letter of them has its wafq, and has its designation within what we have mentioned, because they signify punishment. As for the letters that signify good, the mention of their awfāq and their tables will come hereafter. As for their letters, we have already mentioned them: they are written for everything that has to do with the works of good, because they stand upon the seven planets. And in every wafq we have hinted a subtle symbol, which is understood by one whose custom is understanding from God. And were it not for fear of the ignorant, I would have brought forth what is the hidden pearl; but take what God has apportioned to you, and in what we have mentioned there is sufficiency. And here we have opened the door for whoever wishes to enter. And this is the form of the table of the seven letters, and it is as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

Faṣl. And one of the friends of God said: Whoever wishes that marvels be made manifest to him, and that the hearts of the insolent be made subservient to him, and that the necks of the tyrants bow low before him — let him write what has gone before of the names and the letters and the seven spiritual figures, and let him write this supplication upon a slip 100 times. And let that be after fasting seven consecutive days, and let him recite it by night and by day, and let him speak to no one, and let him not sleep save when overcome. And let him place the slip beneath his head, after he has placed with it something of sweet perfume. Then, after that, he will not approach anyone concerning a need but that it is fulfilled, by the leave of God, exalted is He; and no eye shall behold him but that it loves him. And it is this blessed supplication. You say: O God, there are not in heaven any revolutions, nor in the earth any habitations, nor in the seas any drops, nor in the mountains any clods, nor in the trees any leaves, nor in bodies any motions, nor in eyes any glances, nor in souls any passing thoughts, but that they know You, and bear witness to You, and point to You, and are made subservient within Your kingdom. So by the power whereby You have made subservient all created things, the people of the earths and of the heavens — make subservient to me the hearts of created beings. Truly You have power over all things.

Faṣl. And among what the imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad b. Idrīs al-Rāzī brought out — of what he found excellent — from the library of Hārūn al-Rashīd, /fol. 85v./ from al-Kitāb al-Kabīr al-Jāmiʿ (the Great Comprehensive Book) of the litanies of remembrance and the supplications, he said: Asad b. ʿĀṣim al-Iṣfahānī related to us; he said: Ṣāliḥb. Mihrān related to us, from al-Nuʿmān b. ʿAbd al-Salām, from Abū Yūnus — that is, Mufaḍḍal b. Yūnus — from Muḥammad b. al-Naḍr al-Ḥārithī, who said: There was a man among the devotees of the people of Kufa: when it was the Day of ʿArafa or the Day of Tarwiya, he would perform the major ablution and put on two white garments, then go out to the ẓahr, which is an elevated place of the ground, and supplicate with this supplication; and he would be seen at Mecca or at ʿArafa. And it is this supplication. You say: Hī Sharāhī Hā Ahī Nūr Hī Wāḥid Hī Fard, Quddūs, Quddūs, Quddūs, Lord of Jibrāʾīl and Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl, I ask You by Your name — and You do not disappoint whoever calls upon You. And you ask your need, and God folds up the earth for you thereby. And if you wish, you may supplicate for food and drink, and it will be brought to you, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And that is that you fast in a goodly spiritual retreat (khalwa) for five days, and give three dirhams in alms, and then supplicate with it; and you will see the answer: from whatever thing you have sought, your need comes to you swiftly, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And make good the intention and the inward purpose, and you will encompass what you love. And God knows best.

And by his same chain of transmission, likewise: that there was a man of the devotees of Kufa, and when it was the Day of ʿArafa or the Day of Tarwiya he would perform the major ablution and put on a white garment and a white mantle, then go out to the ẓahr, which is the elevated spot of a mountain or of a hillock — that is to say, a high mound (kudya) — and supplicate with this supplication; and he would be seen at ʿArafa or at Mecca. And it is this blessed supplication. You say: O God, I ask You by Your name — and You do not disappoint whoever calls upon You — by Your name al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), al-Mustaʿān (He whose help is sought), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great), al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted), al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest), al-Bāṭin (the Hidden), al-Maʿbūd (the Worshipped), al-Maḥmūd (the Praised), al-Mubārak (the Blessed), al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent) [the edition prints, al-Mutaqaddir], al-Faḍfāḍ (the Ample). I ask You to fulfil my need. O God, make travel light for me, and fold up the earth for me. And mention whatever you wish of your needs, for you shall be given your request, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. So know the measure of what has reached you, and make your intention and your works sincere: you will find the answer with you, and you will see the marvel of the rending of ordinary courses, and of the fulfilment of needs, and of the swiftness of the answer, by this Greatest Name — the Mighty, the Great, the Swift, the Most Lofty. And they are twelve names, of seven letters save for a little. And if delay befalls you in the answer, it is from your own falling short and the weakness of your certainty; for this is a supplication that does not disappoint anyone who calls with it, certain of the answer, sincere toward God, mighty and majestic is He, but that God, exalted is He, grants him. And none attains that save one who is much-fasting and much-standing in prayer, a keeper of the prayer, of complete religious observance and of true intention. And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said in the Ṣaḥīḥ: ((Let none of you supplicate save while he is certain of the answer.)) And he — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever supplicates while his food is unlawful, and his dwelling unlawful, and his clothing unlawful — how shall he be answered?)) And beware of approaching this supplication save in a [fitting] state and in the stripping off of the filth of this world and of what is unlawful in it; and even were you to fill out your service, it would not fulfil your need — lest you weary your soul and your striving be disappointed, for it is the supplication of the friends of God and of the elect. So understand my counsel to you: you will attain your object and gain your desire. And God's help is sought against /fol. 86r./ what you describe (Q 12:18). And know that the intimate colloquy of the secrets is near, whereas that which bears it, the tongues, is far — save for one to whom God, exalted is He, has brought it near, to him and to his heart. So whoever holds intimate colloquy with the Real by his tongue, the answer comes to him; that is, as God, exalted is He, has said: Those are called from a far place (Q 41:44). And whoever calls upon Him by his inmost secret, He answers him in his inmost secret.
Faṣl: On the Most Beautiful Names of God

His words, blessed and exalted is He: And to God belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them (Q 7:180). And they are: Allāh, there is no god but He; al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), al-Malik (the King), al-Quddūs (the All-Holy), al-Salām (the Peace), al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-ʿAzīz (the

Giver of Life), al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death), al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), al-Wājid (the Finder), al-Mājid (the Glorious), al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Qādir (the Powerful), al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), al-Muqaddim (the Advancer), al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer), al-Awwal (the First), al-Ākhir (the Last), al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest), al-Bāṭin (the A hadith related by al-Tirmidhī and others. And the meaning of "whoever aḥṣāhā" is "memorized them" — thus al-Bukhārī and the majority explained it. And they are in the Mighty Qurʾān in this order.

Abū Zayd ʿUmāra b. Zayd said: Sufyān al-Thawrī related to me, from Ibn ʿUyayna, from Abū l-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra — may God be pleased with him — that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Truly to God belong ninety-nine names, a hundred less one; whoever enumerates them enters the Garden.)) ʿUmāra said: I used to seek them out, and I found no one to inform me of them according to their reality, until I met a man of high aspiration, bent upon the derivation of knowledge from the Family of the House of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace. He had knowledge of the secrets of the letters, and his supplication was answered. And it is said that he would go out from Medina to Mecca in a single day, that day being the Day of ʿArafa, and would witness the standing along with the people, and then return to Medina on the fourth day of the ḥajj. His reports are well known — save that he asked me not to make his name public. And ʿUmāra said: I asked him about the mighty names of God, by which He does not disappoint whoever calls upon Him. And he said to me, after hesitation and refusal: O ʿUmāra, were it not for my trust in you I would not have informed you of them. And they are a trust with you: do not teach them save to one whose religion you approve. O ʿUmāra, they are in the Book of God, exalted is He. And among them, /fol. 86v./ in the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, five names; and in al-Baqara, twenty-five names; and in Āl ʿImrān, three; and in al-Nisāʾ, six; and in al-Anʿām, five names; and in al-Aʿrāf, two; [here the edition prints an unintelligible run of letters:

He said: So I supplicated /fol. 87r./ by these names more than once, and I saw the answer come; and a company wrote them down from me, all of whom informed me that they had recited them at times of grave affairs and calamities, and that God, exalted is He, delivered them from those things by His favour and His generosity. And he said: O ʿUmāra, if you have come to know these names, then you have come to know the Greatest Name of God. So when you resolve to supplicate by them, let it be after a fast; and the fast I most love is that you fast on Thursday, and supplicate by them in the last third of the night of Friday, at the break of the hours before dawn (saḥar). And by God, other than whom there is no god, no believing servant supplicates by these names but that God, exalted is He, answers his supplication — so that, even if he were to ask Him that he might walk upon the water, or upon the surface of the air, God, exalted is He, would answer his supplication.

Know — may God grant success to me and to you — that I have seen, in the handwriting of certain of the gnostics, another way in the manner of supplication. O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh; O God of the first and of the last, Subduer of the rebellious ones and of the tyrants, Abaser of the great ones and of the arrogant. O Lord of the worlds, by Your beneficence we seek help — best Protector and best Helper. O All-Merciful of this world and of the hereafter, Gatherer of the crumbled bones. O Compassionate to the believers, Forgiver of the sin of the disobedient, who makes the unbelievers abide for ever in Hell. O Master of the command on the Day of Judgement, who makes plain that Islam is the religion: be gentle with us on that day, and make us of the people of the prayer and the fast, and lead us along the path of the rightly guided, and … everything … truly You are powerful over everything. O al-Muḥīṭ, O al-Muḥīṭ (the All-Encompassing): Your knowledge has encompassed all knowables, and You have given in full measure, by Your divinity, /fol. 87v./ to those held in bondage, and Your will has gone before within created things. O al-Qādir, O al-Qādir (the Powerful): … Your power over the tyrants among existing things, and so it has appeared in living beings and in inanimate things; and by it subdue the owned and the masters alike. O al-ʿAlīm, O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing) — of particulars and universals, of the terrestrial and the celestial, of existents and knowables. O al-Ḥakīm, O al-Ḥakīm (the Wise): the determinations of Your fashioning have appeared, and thereby has become plain what is due in Your greatness; so there is no escape for great or small from Your bondage. O al-Tawwāb, O al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting) toward those who turn in repentance, O Lord of the worlds and Sovereign of sovereigns: we ask You to raise us to the highest of ʿIlliyyūn, and to string us upon the thread of Your near and beloved ones. O al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing) of our faults — cover them. O al-ʿAlīm of our sins — forgive them. O al-Muḥīṭof our states — order them. O al-Wāsiʿ, O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing): make ample our provisions, and make good our characters, and kindle our longings. O al-Badīʿ, O al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator): give our intellects sight into the wondrousness of the things You have fashioned, and make our hearts firm upon the love of Your Essence and Your attributes, and purify our souls by that which You bestow upon us in unbroken succession. O al-Khallāq, O al-Khallāq (the Creator of all): create in our hearts the awe of Your majesty, and a love [that comes] of putting on Your perfection; and [make] the emblem of the Mighty One the manifesting of Your rites, and the readiness of the heir the very substance of Your glad tidings. O al-Muṣawwir, O al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper): You have given form to the world according to what went before in the precedence of Your will and Your knowledge, and You have made wisdom appear in small and great according to its wisdom and Your wisdom, and You have set it running in the arena of the subduing might of power, so that there is from it neither refuge nor escape. O al-Ghaffār, O al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving): our sins are many, so forgive them; and our faults are numerous, so cover them; and our souls are broken, so mend them; and our satans are rebellious against us, so drive them off. O al-Qahhār, O al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing): You have subdued the servants by death, so that they have from it neither flight nor escape. Before Your omnipotence the necks of the tyrants are humbled, and before Your grandeur the grandeur of the Chosroes has bowed low. O al-Wahhāb, O al-Wahhāb (the Bestower): bestow upon us, within the compass of Your favour, that whereby You may purify our souls, and draw near to Yourself the secret of our hearts and the yearning of our spirits, and illumine with its light our persons, which have grown dark in the eye of existence. O al-Razzāq, O al-Razzāq (the Provider): provide for us out of Your ample treasuries, and continue upon us Your mercy that is near and far-reaching, and continue upon us Your abundant bounty and Your ample favour. O al-Fattāḥ, O al-Fattāḥ (the Opener): open upon us [something] of Your God-given (ladunnī)

sciences, and turn toward us that which preserves us of the splendour of the shining of Your sublime lights, and raise from our inner sights whatever veil has been let down, and bring in upon us the angels with greeting from every gate. O al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor): withhold from us the satanic whisperings, and restrain from us the unbridled rush of the ignorances of human thoughts; and give us delight in the sweetness of Your Book, and write us among the company of Your beloved. O al-Bāsiṭ, O al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander): spread out our provisions, the corporeal and the spiritual, and make wide for us the pavilions of Your delectable secrets, and set us upon the carpet of the expansion of witnessing You, and give us delight in the sweet delectableness of watchful vigilance (murāqaba) toward You. /fol. 88r./ O al-Khāfiḍ, O al-Khāfiḍ (the Abaser): before Your majesty created things have been brought low, and before Your omnipotence originated things have dwindled away; so abase in our enemies whatever harms us, and grant us of well-being and of preservation, in this world and in the hereafter, that which raises us up. O al-Rāfiʿ, O al-Rāfiʿ (the Raiser): raise up the lowly part of our states that has been brought low, and bless what goes unheeded of our works, and strengthen us, and gather us in the company of the near ones among Your righteous beloved, and raise us up with the scribe-angels (al-safara). O al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might): give us might through obedience, and cause us to die upon the way of the Sunna and the Community, and make easy for us the attaining of good things, and keep us from what is great and small of reprehensible deeds. O al-Mudhill (the Giver of abasement): do not abase us with the abasement of acts of disobedience, and give us to enjoy strongholds of

Your love, and provide us with the delight of watchful vigilance toward You, and suffice us against the pain of Your punishment. Truly You are powerful over whatever You will, and worthy [to grant] the answer. And may God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and all his companions, and those who follow them in excellence until the Day of Judgement. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

Faṣl. And know that supplication is the key of worship, and the recourse of the people of want, and the refuge of those driven to extremity, and the reliever of him who has an object of need. Sahl said b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him —: the supplication nearest to being answered is the supplication of [dire] state, which is that its maker be in dire straits. God, exalted is He, said: Or He who answers the one in dire straits when he calls upon Him?(Q 27:62). And know that every soul over which the light of divinity and the radiance of [divine] singling-out predominate — its affinity is of the order of the affinity of the known divine litanies of remembrance. And if darkness predominates over it, and its innate constitution is base, hard, and deficient, then its affinity within the litanies of remembrance is likewise. And so too, if it be a lover of leadership and pre-eminence, it has its own affinity as well. And everyone who takes heed of the states of his own soul knows that he has a determinate course and a determinate way in willing and desiring, in aversion and in dread; and that discipline and spiritual striving do not overcome souls with respect to their divine states and their natural courses. Rather, the effect of discipline and spiritual striving lies only in this, that they weaken those traits of character so that they do not gain mastery over the man. But that a man should be transformed from one quality into another quality — that is impossible. And to this there is an allusion in his words, peace be upon him, ((People are ores, like the ores of gold and silver)), and in his words, ((Spirits are marshalled troops)). So when you have understood this, we say: homogeneity is the cause of conjoining. For every name among the names of God, exalted is He, indicates a determinate meaning; and every soul over which that meaning predominates — that affinity is intensely suited to that name, and it profits by it swiftly.

And there was a certain shaykh — namely Abū l-Najīb al-Baghdādī, may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — who used to command the aspirant to sit before him and to recite over him the Most Beautiful Names once or twice, to the measure that he saw to be of benefit for him, while he looked at his face. And if he saw him devoid of any effect at his reciting them over him, he would say to him: Go out to the market and busy yourself with the concerns of this world, for you have not come out for this path. And if he saw him affected at the hearing of a particular name /fol. 88v./ or of certain determinate names, then he would command him to persevere in that name or those names, since by perseverance the effect increases. And this is what reason requires; for since souls are various, each one of them has a name suited to a particular state. So when those souls occupy themselves with that state which is suited to them, their coming forth from potency is easy and light.

And you may see in a book litanies of remembrance that are unknown. Now the writing may be unknown; yet there is no doubt that writing indicates utterances, and no doubt that utterances indicate the forms in the mind. So those incantations, since they do not indicate anything else — and the second [alternative] is of no avail, because the mention of other than God, exalted is He, avails neither in encouragement nor in deterrence — it remains to say that they indicate the remembrance of God, exalted is He, and the attributes of praise and laudation. For since the divisions of the remembrance of God, exalted is He, are fixed and admit of no increase, the most perfect condition of those words is that they should be of the same kinds as these supplications. As for the divergence that arises from the difference of languages, it is of little effect. It follows necessarily, then, that these known litanies of remembrance are more efficacious in influence than the recitation of the unknown ones.

But someone might say: the souls of most of created beings are defective and deficient. So when they recite these known litanies of remembrance and understand their outward senses, while they have no strong, illumined souls fit to grasp the influences of the divine things, and their souls have not been stripped bare of these corporeal things, then there accrues to their souls from those [litanies] no power and no capacity for producing effect. Whereas when they recite those unknown utterances and do not understand their meanings, and there arise in them the imaginings that it is a lofty word, then terror, fear, and dread take possession of their souls; and there comes to them for this reason a kind of stripping bare from the world of the body and a turning toward the world of holiness; and by this kind of affinity there accrues an increase of power and capacity for producing effect. So this is what I have concerning the unknown incantations. And God knows best.

Faṣl, in which I mention the empty way — that is, the stripping bare of the soul (tajrīd al-nafs) and its attachment — and the special way upon which is the wayfaring of the gnostics, folk who seek the knowledge that leads to the stripping bare of the soul from the world of sense and to its purification apart from natural affairs. And it is proper to some of them and not to others: they are jealous over it, they conceal its matter, and they set their discourse upon it in symbols. And in this they have strange derivations and wondrous skill. And among these is a science, from which [come] the secrets of the letters and the seeking of their aid in the stripping bare of their souls. And among them there is disparity and gradation in the reality of wayfaring, and in the intimate colloquy (najwā) which each one of them employs therein. And that continues to bring near the term of spiritual striving, and the swiftness of arrival at the goal, and the stripping bare of the soul all at once, without hardship and without burden — save for what follows upon that of immense pleasure and complete apprehension. And the reason for their concealing that and their jealousy over it is /fol. 89r./ that, since the stripping bare of the soul by this method [comes] firmly and swiftly, without burden and without great hardship — because of their employing in it various kinds of artifices and of things that assist the one who uses them toward the stripping bare of the soul, even though they have no ultimate aim in the purifying and refining of the soul — as for speaking about these matters: they feared that the wicked might come to know of them and so attain through them to the science of the foolish and to corruption in the earth, since the stripping bare of the soul is the foundation of that. So they concealed this way with all their effort, and left off discussing it altogether. And that at which the shaykhs among the people of verification hinted, and the allusion to it — they set it in symbols and hid it, and turned it toward the side of allusion, of hinting, and of veiled allusion (talwīḥ), rather than of open disclosure and plain declaration. And that is that the wayfarer should set himself to strip bare the powers of his might or the powers of his love, whichever of the two he wishes and toward which his soul inclines. For the soul of man, in their view, has two powers: a power of domination and might, and a power of love and yearning. And the root of these two powers is that the exalted substances, separate from matter, which preside over the principles of existent things and the origin of generated beings — that is, the seven planets (al-darārī al-sabʿ) together with their spheres — each one of them has two states: a state in relation to what is above it, yearning for it, and a state in relation to what is below it. As for that which is in relation to what is above it, it is yearning, love, and passionate love, because of that wherewith the lower is illumined from the light of the higher, and because the higher is a root for the lower and a principle for it; so it is forever set over against it, turned by it toward it, perfected by it, arriving at it through it. And as for that which is in relation to what is below it, it is domination, overcoming, and mastery, because what is below it is in need of it, drawing its supply from it, poor and needing to receive from it of its own accord. And thus, for this reason, the meanings of these two states came to be in all existent things, their high and their low.

And the whole world is ordered out of two paired powers. For there is not found any thing among things but that it has an opposite that stands over against it — such as good and evil, truth and falsehood, light and darkness, male and female, night and day. And all things, when you consider them, you find them all to be paired: their whole and their part, their sensible and their intelligible. And if some part of the existent things in the world is hidden from you upon inspection, that is only because of your deficiency in [the knowledge of] the world and because of your lack of acquaintance with the inward aspects of things. As for the existent things in themselves, they are never free of pairing at all. And that is the meaning of His word, exalted is He, And of everything We created a pair (Q 51:49). So the soul of man has, of the paired power, anger and appetite; and the realization of these two inwardly is domination and love. And the Sufis sometimes name one of these two powers the secret of Majesty (sirr al-jalāl), and the second the secret of Beauty (sirr al-jamāl). So when the gnostic intends to set in motion one of these two psychic powers, he makes his soul feel the meaning that corresponds to that power — of contraction (qabḍ) or of expansion (basṭ) — and sets about the recitation of the litanies of remembrance that befit that meaning and strengthen it, and [he disposes] all the parts of his frame according to its conformity with that secret. So at his recitation of the litany of remembrance he employs the making of a way (taṭrīq) for one of the two meanings and the freeing (taḥrīr) of the second meaning. And he does not cease thus until that meaning takes firm hold within his soul, and its sign appears, and its power prevails over him. And that is the state alluded to among /fol. 89v./ the gnostics; and its reality is an immense power that the person finds within himself at that moment, according to the meaning that is felt. So if it be for domination, he finds within himself a power to collide with all beings and to dominate them — such that, were lions and mighty armies presented to him in that state, he would advance upon them and would not turn aside from them. And if that power be for love and yearning, he finds within himself an immense capacity for attraction and for conjunction with things far removed from him. And these two powers take firm hold, together with their perseverance in setting in motion whichever of the two they wish, until its possession becomes theirs and they attain through it to free disposal in the world of generation however they wish. And when that state has taken firm hold in the soul of the gnostic: if it be for domination, he sets it over the repelling of the corporeal powers, and he seeks help in that by revolving about the centre of his soul. And the soul, meanwhile, is gazing up toward its own world, contemplating what comes upon it from its own quarter. Thereupon the soul is stripped bare of the body with a partial stripping, and sloughs it off with a complete sloughing; and there arises for it an absorption that runs into the matter toward which it is turned. And there comes upon it, from the exalted lights, an influx (wārid) like lightning, exceedingly sweet, which flashes and folds away again in the measure of that state's establishment within the soul.

And if that state be one of love, it turns his yearning and the power of his attraction toward the higher world, and his regard grows slight for what lies behind him of the corporeal powers and their world; and it sloughs itself off from him, and he himself ascends by his own essence, on account of its being stripped bare and sloughed off from the body. And the luminous influx comes upon him with an immense pleasure befitting his state. And he does not cease to summon up that state which he has traversed and upon which he has relied in his turning [to God], until its possession becomes his, such that he no longer has need to summon it. And his thought is absorbed in that influx; he becomes settled with it, his mind does not stray, and he loses all regard for the world of sense entirely. And thereby, at this station, his acquired intellect becomes an active intellect, and he sees his own essence as though it were universal in relation to what is beneath it; and he becomes like the celestial bodies in their lack of the senses and in their turning to the contemplation of the light of God, exalted and hallowed.

So know this section and ponder it with your reason and your mind, and reflect upon its meanings, and you will attain to its riches; for it is the root of this book and its foundation. For the letters are the ground-rule of operative deployment (taṣrīf) in the world of generation, and they have, in the stripping bare of the soul, immense effects in which nothing else can take their place. And he who knows their secrets

— when he directs himself by each letter of them toward the thing that corresponds to it, until the shape of the letter and its corporeal form are effaced from his thought and its spiritual form dawns upon him: then at that moment the occult property of that letter becomes manifest to him. And when the repeater repeats them with his heart and his tongue many times over, they engender in the soul a power of might, of subduing, of expansion, and of attraction. And God, exalted is He, is the One whose help is sought, and to Him is the return.

Faṣl. And know that the ranks of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) — may God be pleased with them — are that the reality of the Hereafter be unveiled to them, and what God, exalted is He, has prepared therein for its people, and that they behold /fol. 90r./ the everlasting bliss. The first thing with which God, exalted is He, favours them is the word of divine oneness (kalimat al-tawḥīd), which is: "There is no god but God" — glorified is He — and it is 12 letters; and that is for the absolute Command. As for the operative deployment (taṣrīf) of its relation within the engendered beings, it is by the manifestation of "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God", and this too is 12 letters; and by it the operative deployment within the engendered beings subsists. That one, then, is for bringing into existence, and this one is for operative deployment. And you are the one who gathers the two realities, who contains the two worlds, who witnesses the two abodes. So take to steadfastness upon the secret of that. And know that the spirit — God, exalted is He, created it from the weakness of a thing and lodged it in bodies, so that it grew weak from the darkness of the natural moulds, composite and essential.

Then God, exalted is He, favoured it with the names and their lights, and commanded it to rise in its ladder of ascent (miʿrāj) and to climb to its degrees. And if it stands fast until it dies to its regarding of bodies, and not by neighbouring them, and comes forth from the bondage of worship, God, exalted is He, gives it life by a spirit from among the spirits of His holiness; and there appears to it the unveiling of the wonders of the Dominion (malakūt) and the subtleties of the Omnipotence (jabarūt). That is another genesis in respect of the spirit.

Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: The forebears (al-salaf) — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — are agreed that the limit of the Lordly opening (al-fatḥal-rabbānī) and of the unveiling of divine bestowal (al-kashf al-mawhibī) is not sound for one in whose stomach is the weight of a mote of food; and that is the limit of corporeal self-sufficiency (al-ṣamadāniyya al-jismāniyya). And whoever multiplies [the invocation of] His name al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent) is granted awe in the world and the acceptance of his speech, if he has a truthful aspiration (himma); for God, exalted is He, subjugates to him the kinds of the world by the secret of subjugation, because the lights of Magnificence revert upon it and then revert upon [all] other than him — so everyone who sees him holds him in awe, and everyone who sits with him finds increase. Just so, when he multiplies [the invocation of] His name al-Nūr (the Light), God bestows upon him the realities of this name, until he beholds the light of God, exalted is He, and what He has brought into being in the luminous worlds, such as the angels brought near and the spirits of those brought near. And the light of the Qurʾān: all of it is light. When he utters it, it comes forth as light; and when he recites it in secret, he sees the light — how it threads through the parts of the body, then pierces the air, then pierces the heavens, then pierces the Footstool, then pierces the Throne, then that light vanishes into its own hiddenness, so that he does not know where it has ended. This is a state that comes upon the reciters, the people of light; and they remain ever between sobriety (ṣaḥw) and intoxication (sukr). If they travel by the outward, they behold the lights of the engendered beings, and so they are the people of sobriety; and if they travel by the inward, they behold the lights of Beauty, and so they are the people of sobriety and intoxication. And by this luminous Name ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — pierced through, when he saw what was conveyed to him concerning Sāriya, in the traversing of the distance by the power of the light of faith. And by it the Chosen One (al-Muṣṭafā) — God bless him and grant him peace — beheld every piercing-through: such as the Garden [seen] in the walled orchard of the Banū al-Najjār, and such as the earth, of which the dominion of his community shall attain what was folded up for him. And let him renew the ablution for every prayer, and let him not incline to what exceeds his own station among the kinds of lights, except such as he has witnessed therein of the realities of faith. And among the supplications of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — was: ((O God, make for me a light in my heart, and a light in my thought, and a light in my hearing, and a light in my sight, and a light in my hair, and a light in my skin, and a light in my flesh, and a light in my blood, and a light in my bone, and a light before me, and a light behind me, and a light on my right, and a light on my left, and a light above me, and a light beneath me. O God, /fol. 90v./ increase me in light, and give me light, and make for me light.)) And whoever God, exalted is He, has granted the unveiling of this light, and for whom He has unveiled the secrets of the Hereafter — he it is whom God, exalted is He, will comfort thereby in his grave, and he will be raised up together with it. God, exalted is He, has said: On a day when God will not put to shame the Prophet and those who have believed with him — their light speeding onward before them and at their right hands — they say: Our Lord, complete for us our light— by the light of Your noble Face — and forgive us (Q 66:8). For we have sought it only by a mercy from You, since the light of the believers is a veil between them and the light of God, exalted is He. And by that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — described our Lord to us, saying: ((His veil is light; and were it not for that light, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reached.)) And the Throne is from the light of God, exalted is He; and the Footstool is from the light of the Throne; and the cherubim are from the light of the Footstool; and the angels ranged in ranks are from the light of the Pen; and the angels who glorify are from the light of the Tablet; and the angels of operative deployment are from the light of the Footstool; and the Omnipotence is from the light of the heavens and the earth — and it is the isthmus (barzakh) that lies between the heavens and the earth, and it is the lower Omnipotence, and above it is the higher Omnipotence; and the earth is from the Omnipotence; and the Omnipotence is from the light of the angel; and the plant is from the light of the animal; and the inanimate is from the light of the plant; and the plant is from the light of man; and man is from the light of the Throne. So the matter came full circle, returning upon his hands — I mean the believer to whom the reality of this name has been unveiled. So whoever has had its light unveiled to him understands what the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — pointed to in his hadith: ((It has come round as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth)) — the hadith in its full length; meaning the year. For in the Jāhiliyya they used to make Ṣafar the sacred month, according to His words, exalted is He: they make it lawful one year and forbid it another year (Q 9:37). So when Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — came, he abrogated [that] and restored the month of God, al-Muḥarram, to its place and its seat; and the matter returns to what God, exalted is He, had determined and named, and He made it the first of the months of the year on the day He created the heavens and the earth. This, then, is the meaning of "it has come round". And likewise man: he was created from the light of the Throne, and to it he returned. So understand. And our aim in this is not to draw attention to the steps of gradation, but only that he may behold that within himself; for within him, from the light of the Throne, is the intellect; and from the light of the Footstool, tenderness; and from the light of the Pen, the spirit; and from the light of the Tablet, the soul.

Faṣl, in which I mention this noble verse and … and its wafq. It is His words, exalted is He: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills; and God is the Possessor of mighty bounty (Q 3:73–74). This verse is for the amplitude of provision. And for one who wishes to seek women in marriage: you write it on Thursday upon a sheet, and he wraps it in a rag from the shirt of a fortunate man and hangs it upon the door of his shop, or the place of his selling or of his buying, or a dwelling of his — then its good is granted him as provision, and God, exalted is He, provides for him, and provision is guided toward him. And if it is written in a new vessel and one who desires repentance and turning back [to God] drinks it, he repents /fol. 91r./ and turns back from what he is in; and the means and the things sought are made easy for him, and God, exalted is He, provides for him from whence he does not reckon. And in that is a wondrous secret for those who seek the means. And if it is written with the conditions previously mentioned and placed among goods and merchandise, then God, exalted is He, makes blessing appear in them, with the best selling and the greatest price; and that is by the blessing of this noble verse. So understand. And God speaks the truth and guides to the way. And this is the form of the wafq, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

So whoever recites this noble verse 12 times on Friday after the … prayer, God — glorified and exalted — provides for him from whence he does not reckon, and he will not see want during that week. And that is [to be done] with sincerity, conviction, excellence, complete directedness, and perfect purity, outwardly and inwardly. And when he recites it, let him hold firm in his heart that there is none who withholds and none who gives but God, exalted is He, and that he recites it relying upon God with truthfulness and directedness. And that will be by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Faṣl, on His words, exalted is He: When the wife of ʿImrān said: My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, consecrated; so accept it from me. Indeed You, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And when she gave birth to her, she said: My Lord, I have given birth to a female — and God knew best what she had borne, and the male is not like the female — and I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her and her offspring /fol. 91v./ in [You] from the accursed Satan. So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance, and caused her to grow with a goodly growth, and Zakariyyāʾ took charge of her. Whenever Zakariyyāʾ entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found provision with her. He said: O Maryam, from where does this come to you? She said: It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning (Q 3:35–37). The occult property of this noble verse is for pregnant women: a safeguard for their children against afflictions, and a help toward their rearing. And if these verses are written with musk and saffron upon gazelle parchment and hung upon the woman's right upper arm until the time of her delivery, then she is preserved from afflictions. And if it is written with musk and saffron and hung upon the child's neck in a new tube, then it is a mighty amulet against weeping, distress, and terror; his wakefulness is lessened, and it suffices him against his ailments. And it is said that he will be of blessed and goodly growth. And this noble and honoured verse has, of number, 5994; and there corresponds to this number, among the awfāq, the square of the letter (fāʾ). Its opener (miftāḥ) is 626 and its closer (mighlāq) is 756; and to it belongs, among the zodiacal signs, Virgo (al-Sunbula), and its manifester is Mercury (ʿUṭārid). And God, blessed and exalted, knows best. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

An account of the words of Adam — peace be upon him — with which he supplicated when he was cast down to the earth from the Garden. God, exalted is He, inspired him to supplicate with these words; and he supplicated with them, and He turned toward him in forgiveness. And no one weighed down with care has supplicated with them but that God, exalted is He, relieved his care and lifted it from him; and no one having a need has supplicated with them but that God, exalted is He, fulfilled his need. /fol. 92r./ And they are these words: There is no god but You; glory be to You; I have done evil and wronged myself; I have confessed my sin, so forgive me my sins, for none forgives sins but You, the All-Forgiving, the Compassionate. O God, I ask You and seek access to You by the highest light, which I found written upon the pavilions of the Throne and upon the gates of the Garden — and it is the light of Your prophet Muḥammad, to whom You have conjoined Your name — O God, O God, O Lord of the worlds.
And this is what has been concluded of the chapter. And God, exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
